extracted.intended_audience: federal agencies' NEPA practitioners, environmental compliance officers, and legal/regulatory staff responsible for establishing, substantiating, or applying categorical exclusions (CEs) under NEPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for how agencies should establish, substantiate, apply, document, jointly create, programmatically create, adopt, and publish categorical exclusions (CEs) under the NEPA regulations, including handling extraordinary circumstances, mitigation, expiration criteria, and public/CEQ coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of individual and aggregate effects when establishing CEs
rubrics_metrics.description: When establishing a CE, an agency must determine that the application of the CE to a single action and the repeated collective application to multiple actions would not have significant effects — i.e., the category of actions covered by the CE does not significantly affect the human environment "individually or in the aggregate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ chose the phrase "in the aggregate" (rather than "cumulatively") to avoid confusion, and notes the regulations' definition of "effects" includes direct, indirect, and cumulative effects. Agencies must consider both the effects of an individual action and the aggregated effects of anticipated multiple actions covered by the CE. All effects analyses are bounded by reasonable foreseeability. Agencies have flexibility in how to evaluate whether aggregate applications will not ordinarily have significant effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiate CEs at establishment (not at each application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must consider whether a category of actions normally does not have a significant effect "individually or in the aggregate" at the time the agency establishes and substantiates the CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ explains agencies are not required to analyze aggregate effects each time they apply a CE except to the extent the agency's extraordinary circumstances review requires such an analysis; requiring an analysis at each application (independent of extraordinary circumstances) would undermine CE efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extraordinary circumstances standard for applying a CE
rubrics_metrics.description: If extraordinary circumstances exist for a particular action, the agency must conduct an analysis and make an affirmative determination that the proposed action does not in fact have the potential to result in significant effects notwithstanding the extraordinary circumstance, or the agency must modify the action to avoid the potential to result in significant effects; if it cannot, the agency must prepare an EA or EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ revised paragraph (b)(1) to require an affirmative demonstration that there is no potential for significant effects to apply a CE when extraordinary circumstances are present. The agency may modify the action to "avoid" potential significant effects (not rely on compensatory mitigation to justify application of the CE). This standard aligns with agency practice and case law and prevents application of CEs where only case-by-case mitigation (after the fact) would otherwise be relied on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required when applying a CE notwithstanding extraordinary circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency identifies extraordinary circumstances but nevertheless determines that application of the CE is appropriate (either via analysis showing no potential for significant effects or by modifying the action to avoid the potential), the agency must document that determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation is required only in instances where the agency identifies extraordinary circumstances but still applies the CE; CEQ encourages, but does not require, publication of such documentation to avoid burdens on agency resources. The documentation requirement applies to both (1) when an analysis shows no potential for significant effects despite extraordinary circumstances and (2) when an agency modifies the action to avoid potential significant effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modifications must avoid potential effects, not compensate
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency modifies a proposed action to address an extraordinary circumstance to permit application of a CE, the modification must "avoid the potential to result in significant effects" rather than compensate for such effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ clarifies that reliance on compensatory mitigation as the basis to apply a CE in the presence of extraordinary circumstances is inappropriate; other NEPA provisions (e.g., mitigated FONSI allowances) may permit compensatory mitigation in other contexts, but not as the basis for CE application in extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies may establish CEs jointly
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may establish categorical exclusions individually or jointly with other agencies, including using a shared substantiation document and listing the CE in each agency's NEPA procedures or other joint documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint establishment can save administrative time, reduce redundancy, and improve cohesion. The requirement to substantiate CEs (including public review and comment) applies equally to joint CEs as to those established by a single agency. CEQ notes the NEPA regulations never prohibited joint establishment and adds language to clarify acceptability and transparency expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing CEs through programmatic or planning decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may establish CEs through a land use plan, a decision document supported by a programmatic EIS or EA, or other equivalent planning or programmatic decisions supported by an environmental document prepared under NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is optional and intended to encourage programmatic and planning reviews that can substantiate CEs tailored to specific contexts, geographies, or project types, and can reduce duplication (e.g., avoid revising NEPA procedures after a programmatic EIS). Once established, these CEs may be applied to future site-specific or project-level actions addressed in the program or plan. CEQ clarified that "other equivalent planning or programmatic decision" requires support by a NEPA environmental document.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEQ review and public comment for programmatic CE establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: When agencies establish CEs through programmatic or planning documents, agencies must provide CEQ an opportunity to review and comment and provide opportunities for public comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may satisfy the notification and comment requirement by incorporating the proposed CEs into any interagency and public review process applicable to the programmatic or planning document. CEQ declined to impose a strict timeline for its review but will strive for prompt comments. Coordination with CEQ facilitates consistency across government and helps ensure adequate substantiation of CEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantiation and extraordinary-circumstances requirements for programmatic CEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Programmatically established CEs must meet the same requirements to substantiate that the category of actions covered by a CE normally will not result in significant effects (individually or in the aggregate) and must identify extraordinary circumstances, consistent with requirements for CEs established under agency NEPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies have flexibility in how they identify or compile the list of extraordinary circumstances (e.g., rely on their NEPA procedures' list, create a list specific to the programmatic CE, or combine approaches). Agencies may document compliance with these requirements in the relevant programmatic or planning documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for determining CE applicability to specific actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must establish a process for determining that a CE applies to a specific action in the absence of extraordinary circumstances or determines the CE still applies notwithstanding extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process is part of the programmatic CE establishment requirements and helps ensure consistent, transparent application of the CE at the project level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and publish a list of all CEs on agency websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must maintain a list of all CEs established under the alternative programmatic mechanism on their websites, similar to requirements for CEs established in agency NEPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ encourages agencies to list all agency CEs in a single location, regardless of how they were established, to provide public transparency and easy access. Agency websites should clearly link the CEs to their underlying programmatic or planning documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow CEs that are geographically or characteristic-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may establish CEs that cover specific geographic areas or areas that share common characteristics (e.g., a specific habitat type for a given species).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such CEs were added as examples of features agencies may consider when establishing CEs and were included without specific adverse comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow limited-duration (time-limited) CEs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may establish CEs for limited durations when doing so enables narrowing the scope of analysis necessary to substantiate that a class of activities normally will not have significant environmental effects, especially where future uncertainty exists or frequency of actions may increase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should periodically review the continued validity of limited-duration CEs consistent with the CE review timeframe in §1507.3(c)(9). Once the limited duration threshold is met, agencies may consider the CE expired, conduct additional analysis to create a permanent CE, or reissue the CE if adequately substantiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEs may incorporate mitigation measures as part of the category (mitigated CEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CE may include mitigation measures integrated into the category of action itself; mitigation incorporated into a CE must be adopted through the public comment process and implemented as part of the activity for the CE to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation integrated into the CE is not the same as case-by-case mitigation used to compensate for effects after the fact. Agencies cannot rely on compensatory mitigation to justify applying a CE in the presence of extraordinary circumstances. Where mitigation is part of a CE, the agency must determine that implementation of the mitigation will ensure the category of activities will not normally have a significant effect. Examples include restoring or conserving equivalent habitat or reducing sediment from other sources. Agencies must include the mitigation in their proposed actions for the CE to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEs may include expiration criteria or thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may include criteria in a CE that would cause it to expire — e.g., a specified number of acres, occurrences, or an expiration date — beyond which the agency may no longer apply the CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expiration criteria can reduce the difficulty of substantiating a CE by limiting its scope. Agencies determine whether such criteria are mandatory or discretionary when establishing the CE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption/use of another agency's CE limited to administratively established CEs (not legislative)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adopting agency may adopt and apply another agency's CE consistent with section 109 of NEPA only where the CE was administratively established by the agency (including CEs Congress directs agencies to establish administratively); the provision does not permit adoption of legislative CEs created directly by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ encourages agencies to include legislative CEs established by statute in their NEPA procedures for transparency, but the adoption provision does not apply to those legislative CEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopting agency must identify the proposed action or category when adopting another agency's CE
rubrics_metrics.description: When adopting another agency's CE, the adopting agency must identify the proposed action or category of proposed actions that falls within the CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identification is required by proposed paragraph (e)(1) to ensure clarity about the scope of adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopting agency must consult with the establishing agency
rubrics_metrics.description: The adopting agency must consult with the agency that established the CE, consistent with section 109(2) of NEPA, to ensure the CE is appropriate for the proposed action(s) and to follow any processes contemplated in the establishing agency's procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation helps ensure the adopting agency understands any conditions or factors the establishing agency requires (e.g., lists of conditions to apply the CE, documentation requirements). Internal establishing-agency procedures unrelated to proper application of the CE (e.g., internal legal review protocols) do not bind the adopting agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopting agency must evaluate extraordinary circumstances and explain its process
rubrics_metrics.description: The adopting agency must evaluate the proposed action for extraordinary circumstances when applying an adopted CE and must explain the process it will use to evaluate extraordinary circumstances (including whether it will apply the establishing agency's extraordinary circumstances, its own, or both).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ declined to prescribe which agency's extraordinary-circumstances list governs; instead, the adopting agency should describe how it will address extraordinary circumstances in its public notification. Agencies should discuss during consultation how the adopting agency will review for extraordinary circumstances, taking into account definitions and requirements in each agency's NEPA procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public notification required when adopting another agency's CE (adoption, not each application)
rubrics_metrics.description: An adopting agency must provide public notification when it is adopting another agency's CE for a proposed action or category of actions, including a brief description of the proposed action(s) and the process for consideration of extraordinary circumstances and a brief description of the consultation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 109(3) of NEPA requires public notice of CE adoption. CEQ uses the term "public notification" and clarifies this notice concerns adoption of a CE (not notice for each individual project under the adopted CE). CEQ declines to require agencies to solicit formal public comment on adoption, though it encourages comment in appropriate cases when community interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopting agency should publish documentation of the application of the adopted CE
rubrics_metrics.description: The adopting agency is required to publish the documentation of the adopting agency's application of the adopted CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ proposed (and includes) a requirement that the adopting agency publish documentation of the application of the CE to provide transparency about use of adopted CEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain use of word 'normally' in describing CEs
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations retain the qualifier "normally" in describing categorical exclusions — i.e., CEs identify categories of actions that normally do not have significant environmental effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEQ retained this term for consistency with the 2020 rule and Phase 2 responses; commenters had opposed the term but CEQ kept it for reasons discussed elsewhere in the rulemaking.
